entries.work: Wurgaft et al., Manifold Steering Reveals the Shared Geometry of Neural Network Representation and Behavior (arXiv 2605.05115, ICML 2026)
entries.one_line: Fits an activation manifold and tests a CAUSAL link to a behaviour manifold by steering; TP-G2 is a correlational placement test on a kNN-geodesic map of code states with a factorial mechanism-vs-surface decoupling and no intervention.
entries.quote: we find that steering along $M_h$, which we term manifold steering, yields behavioral trajectories that follow $M_y$

entries.work: Schutt, Kipnis, Diedrichsen and Kriegeskorte, Statistical inference on representational geometries (eLife 2023; arXiv 2112.09200)
entries.one_line: Two-factor cross-validation + bootstrap for RSA model comparison; TP-G2 bootstraps programs within cells (graph rebuilt) and reports a split-half cross-validated centroid distance as a sensitivity.
entries.quote: Our inference methods combine novel 2-factor extensions of crossvalidation (to prevent overfitting to either subjects or conditions from inflating our estimates of model accuracy) and bootstrapping

entries.work: Hewitt and Liang, Designing and Interpreting Probes with Control Tasks (EMNLP 2019; arXiv 1909.03368)
entries.one_line: Selectivity = real-task minus control-task performance; TP-G2 runs lexical baselines (block-0 state, TF-IDF tokens, AST n-grams) through the identical RSA pipeline and reports selectivity = rho_d(model) - rho_d(baseline), which is negative here.
entries.quote: a good probe, (one that reflects the representation), should be selective, achieving high linguistic task accuracy and low control task accuracy

entries.work: Ahmed, Yu, Huang, Wang, Devanbu and Sagae, Towards Understanding What Code Language Models Learned (arXiv 2306.11943; cited in the plan as 'Ma et al.')
entries.one_line: Reports that code models capture computational semantics beyond surface form; TP-G2 finds that for search-algorithm DISCIPLINE the Qwen3 program map at the frozen M-code readout follows code surface (container, AST shingles, length) and carries no more discipline information than lexical baselines.
entries.quote: we investigate their ability to capture semantics of code beyond superficial frequency and co-occurrence

entries.work: Guillot and Rousset, Dismantling the Mantel tests (Methods Ecol. Evol. 2013; arXiv 1112.0651)
entries.one_line: Partial Mantel tests with full label permutation are not valid when variables are structured; TP-G2 permutes discipline labels only within container (and container within discipline), with type-I rate 0.055 in its synthetic check (T4).
entries.quote: We show that contrarily to a widely shared belief, partial Mantel tests are not valid in this case, and their bias remains close to that of the simple Mantel test.

entries.work: Neuron-Guided Interpretation of Code LLMs: Where, Why, and How? (arXiv 2512.19980)
entries.one_line: RSA semantic probe + AST syntactic probe; reports middle-layer 'concept layers'. TP-G2's frozen readout sits at middle depth (8B block 17/36, 32B block 33/64) yet its cell geometry for algorithm discipline is dominated by surface; the nearby blocks L-2..L+2 give the same picture.
entries.quote: lower layers mainly encode language-specific syntax, while middle layers capture semantic abstractions shared across languages, emerging as concept layers

entries.work: Jin and Rinard, Emergent Representations of Program Semantics in Language Models Trained on Programs (arXiv 2305.11169)
entries.one_line: Probes recover program states in a grid-world language with an interventional baseline; TP-G2 is about algorithm-level discipline in natural Python search code and is correlational.
entries.quote: a novel interventional baseline that disambiguates what is represented by the LM as opposed to learned by the probe

note: No found work runs a factorial discipline x container decoupling of LLM program representations with restricted-permutation RSA; the closest (2306.11943, 2512.19980) report semantic organisation that TP-G2 does not find for algorithm discipline at this readout.
